notes:
Summary: Solstice is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for core inference across their digital workplace features (in-app assistant, enterprise search, code helper). Primary drivers: predictable latency, cost control, and VPC-based deployment. They have strict EU data residency needs for a subset of clients and want on-prem options for regulated lines.

Cost modelling and reserved capacity discussion (high-value CRM notes / fragments):
- Customer target throughput: ~600 req/s peak across 3 regions, baseline steady-state 250-300 req/s.
- Latency SLO targets: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms for chat; reranking tighter p95 <= 80ms for short-context queries.
- Proposed reserved commit: initial 24 x A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed 80GB/40GB packing plan). Customer asked for clear mapping: 24 reserved ~= sustained 400-700 req/s depending on batching and token mix.
- Utilization assumptions used in model: 65% steady-state utilization, 85% peak packing with autoscale/burst allowances.
- Token assumptions: average tokens per request = 120 (prompt + completion mix), monthly token estimate = 1.2B tokens. Customer emphasized many short queries (quick questions) that raise overhead for p95 latency.
- Unit economics from Redwood draft model:
  - On-demand per-1k tokens baseline (hosted) = $0.0050
  - Reserved-commit blended unit after 12mo commit (with quantization & batching) = $0.0025 per 1k tokens
  - Break-even commit level estimated at ~18 GPUs for current workload; incremental savings beyond 36 GPUs flatten due to diminishing returns on packing.
- Commit tiers discussed in pricing doc: 6-month (10% discount), 12-month (25% discount), 24-month (33% discount) + optional burst credits. Customer pushing for additional 5% for multi-year.
- Billing granularity debate: customer prefers monthly true-up (so they only pay for reserved vs actual utilization difference monthly). Redwood team prefers monthly invoice with quarterly re-evaluation.
- SLA negotiation points on table:
  - SLOs guaranteed per-route (chat vs embeddings vs rerank) with separate p95/p99 targets.
  - SLA credits for missed latency/availability windows; customer requests a ramp schedule (less strict first 3 months while optimizing).
  - Legal wants caps on credits, rollback options if infra fails; Solstice wants stronger uptime credits and faster incident escalation (1-hour P1 response SLA).
- Technical levers called out to hit unit economics:
  - Aggressive quantization (int8) for mid-sized models to increase packing density.
  - KV cache for prefixes and common prompts to lower token generation for repeated flows.
  - Adaptive batching windows tuned per route to keep p95 under target while maximizing throughput.
- POC success criteria:
  - Sustain 250 qps steady-state with p95 <= 120ms on representative workload.
  - Demonstrate 30-40% unit cost reduction after quantization & packing compared to stock runtime.
  - Show deterministic fallback behavior to hosted API with <2x latency and documented cost impact.

Quotes / snippets from Solstice stakeholders:
- "We need a predictable monthly bill and SLOs that scale with our growth—can't have surprise token surges killing margins." - Head of Platform
- "If you can show stable p95 < 120ms with our corpus and a 12-month commit that materially lowers cost per token, we can move to procurement." - VP of Engineering

Open items / next steps (CRM actions):
- SE (Jordan) to deliver revised cost model using 12-mo and 24-mo commit scenarios with hourly vs monthly billing rows (due 2026-03-18).
- AE (Maya) to coordinate legal for SLA language draft and data residency annex; target internal review by 2026-03-25.

- Confirm EU data residency attestation document and provide SOC2 Type II report (linked in drive). Legal ticket SEC-1289 remains open.
- Customer requested an explicit demo of burst behavior and fallback to hosted API; schedule week of 2026-03-22.

Stakes: high — Solstice is an anchor customer possibility (enterprise footprint + potential to expand to 3 internal business units). If pricing and SLA align, expected ARR mid-six figures first year and growth to low seven figures with additional seats and regions.
